sections.heading: Learner licence and preparation
sections.text: Delhi public guidance describes a learner licence as temporary and valid for up to six months. It also directs learners to prepare on vehicle controls, road signs, and traffic rules.

sections.heading: Permanent licence timing
sections.text: Delhi public guidance says a valid learner licence must be held for at least 30 days before the competence test, and the permanent licence application should be made within six months of learner-licence issue.

sections.heading: Appointments and fees
sections.text: Delhi public guidance identifies appointment and fee payment as driving-licence service topics. Current availability, fee amounts, and any transaction must be checked in the approved public source; DigiLicense does not carry out that transaction.

sections.heading: Renewal and replacement
sections.text: Delhi public guidance lists renewal and duplicate-licence requirements separately. This corpus is reference material only and does not determine an applicant's eligibility or submit a request.

sections.heading: Permanent driving-licence fee
sections.text: The reviewed Delhi public permanent driving-licence page lists a revised fee of 400 Indian rupees, including the smart-card amount shown there. Fees can change, and DigiLicense does not accept payment.

sections.heading: Learner's licence
sections.text: The learner's-licence workflow guides a user through the form, recorded submission, fee step, and next action shown by DigiLicense. It is simulated prototype behavior and does not submit an official application or decide legal eligibility.

sections.heading: Learner's test
sections.text: The learner's-test workflow provides a preparation checklist, an in-product test, and a recorded result. It is simulated prototype behavior; passing it does not create an official learner licence.

sections.heading: Permanent driving licence
sections.text: The permanent-driving-licence workflow explains displayed eligibility dates or locked actions, records the form and fee steps, and leads to appointment preferences. It is simulated prototype behavior and neither decides legal eligibility nor submits an official application.

sections.heading: Renewal
sections.text: The renewal workflow records its guided form, displayed fee action, and status inside DigiLicense. It is simulated prototype behavior and does not renew an official driving licence.

sections.heading: Duplicate or replacement
sections.text: The duplicate-or-replacement workflow records its guided request and status inside DigiLicense. It is simulated prototype behavior and does not issue or replace an official driving licence.

sections.heading: Change of address
sections.text: The change-of-address workflow records local verification, proof, review, and status steps. It is simulated prototype behavior and does not alter a government record.

sections.heading: Mobile-number update
sections.text: The mobile-update workflow records local verification and status. Its optional mock Aadhaar proof is simulated prototype behavior; DigiLicense does not contact Aadhaar or change a government record.

sections.heading: Application status
sections.text: The application-status workflow explains only persisted synthetic DigiLicense records and their displayed reason codes. It is simulated prototype behavior and cannot inspect a government system.

sections.heading: Fees and payment
sections.text: The fee catalogue and payment result are recorded only inside DigiLicense. Payment is a simulated workflow: no real money is charged and no government fee is confirmed.

sections.heading: Appointment waitlist and offers
sections.text: The appointment workflow records zone and delivery preferences, waitlist membership, offer timers, and confirmation inside DigiLicense. Appointment reservation is a simulated workflow and does not reserve a real appointment.

sections.heading: Assistant scope and fallback
sections.text: The assistant explains only these ten DigiLicense workflows from reviewed prototype evidence. It does not provide real-world policy, legal advice, government links, or general knowledge. If the evidence is insufficient, it returns bounded DigiLicense guidance instead of guessing.
